body:
Good morning, Kern County. It's Wednesday, September 2, and while crews are just starting day two of the big Hageman Road construction project that has businesses and commuters bracing for a month of delays, the valley itself is waking up mild and calm — expect a high near 82 today with moderate air quality and no active alerts. There's a lot to get to this morning, from a night of scattered incidents across the county to a deeper look at why the long-predicted wave of baby boomers selling their homes hasn't materialized, so let's get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy but thankfully non-fatal night across Kern County, with the most serious call coming just after midnight on Highway 58. Around 12:41 a.m., a rollover crash on westbound 58 west of Tucker Road drew a multi-unit response including a battalion chief, with an air unit standing by. Westbound lanes were reduced while crews worked the scene, though the extent of any injuries has not been released.

Just over an hour later, at roughly 1:48 a.m., dispatchers sent officers to a home in the Coburn Ridge area on reports of five to six shots fired. Callers said subjects in ski masks had been seen at the door, and the reporting party was pulling camera footage as a vehicle fled the area. Officers responded to the scene.

Elsewhere around the county, crews knocked down a grass fire off Wasco Pond Road north of Cecil Avenue around 1:30 a.m., with fire progression stopped after an engine, patrol unit, and additional help arrived. In Bakersfield, a short foot pursuit of a man on a dirt bike along a Chester Avenue bike path ended around 9:58 p.m. when visual contact was lost near Chester; units were searching the area. Earlier in the evening, a call at Virginia Avenue and Powell Street reported a male subject making threats to obtain a firearm, drawing additional officers to the scene.

The overnight log also included a steady run of welfare checks and mental health calls — a 17-year-old on Marble Street reported making suicidal statements around 10:48 p.m. drew officers and medics, a female in crisis on the West China Grade was attended to around 10:44 p.m., and a welfare check was conducted for a 15-year-old reported missing and last seen near Bernard Street just after midnight. Crews also handled a CHP-reported roadside fire on northbound Highway 99 south of Olive Drive at 9:32 p.m., and a report of a vehicle fire on Elk Hills Road at 11:32 p.m. that turned out to be a dropped flare with no active fire.

## Today's weather

It's a mild start to September out there. The current observation at Meadows Field is 61 degrees, with today's high expected to reach only 82 and tonight's low dipping to around 60. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and the clear conditions should hold through the day. Air quality sits at 53, which is moderate — fine for most people, though those sensitive to particulates may want to keep outdoor exertion light. Monday's heat has broken, and it looks like a pleasant, seasonable stretch ahead. No active fires are being tracked locally.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a major road construction project on Hageman Road launched Monday at 7 a.m. and will continue daily until 7 p.m. through the end of September.** The city says the work is necessary, but businesses along the corridor are already feeling it — a waitress at Slice of Italy told the station customers are struggling to get to the restaurant, and neighboring businesses said they wish the city had given clearer advance notice. Residents, like Tina DiStefano, are worried about traffic congestion and school drop-off delays, while others like Brent Andrews acknowledge the long-anticipated work was inevitable.

**KGET 17 reports that the Shafter City Council has approved an ordinance banning sleeping in public.** The measure passed amid ongoing debate over how to address homelessness in the small Kern County city. Details on enforcement and any available alternatives for those affected have not been fully detailed, but the vote signals a harder line from local leaders as encampment complaints have risen across the region.

**According to 23ABC, the long-predicted "silver tsunami" has never arrived — and that's tightening the housing market for younger Kern County families.** Bakersfield Association of Realtors president Paris Davis told the station that many baby boomers are staying in larger homes due to paid-off mortgages, locked-in low interest rates, and the difficulty of downsizing from a 4,000-square-foot house to something smaller. Economics professor Aaron Hegde added that boomers own about 35% of three-bedroom-or-larger homes in the U.S., but he says the bigger driver of high prices is an overall housing shortage, not boomers staying put.

**23ABC also reports that Kern County is facing a serious shortage of attorneys, just as California considers expanding access to civil legal help.** Greater Bakersfield Legal Assistance calls the county a "legal desert," with only 0.9 attorneys for every 1,000 residents. The organization receives 500 to 700 calls weekly and saw its caseload jump 41% from 2022 to 2025. Kassie Mullican, GBLA's director of community development, said the lack of capacity and funding means more people are navigating civil cases on their own; one client, Mehru Khan, shared that GBLA's help was critical in obtaining a restraining order during a domestic violence situation.

**Bakersfield Now reports that two lanes have reopened on southbound I-5 near Grapevine Road.** The lanes had been closed following an earlier incident, and CHP confirmed they were back open, which should ease southbound travel through the Grapevine corridor today.

**KGET 17 reports on an unlikely new addition to Bakersfield College's football program — a starting quarterback who came all the way from Melbourne, Australia.** The story highlights how the Renegades found their signal-caller from halfway around the world, an interesting footnote to the local sports scene as fall practices get underway.

## Something good

There's a bit of welcome news in the arts world this week — KGET 17 reports that the Portrait of a Warrior Gallery is moving to a new location and will become a neighbor to Woolworth's next year. It's an exciting new chapter for the gallery and a nice addition to a downtown block that's been growing steadily.

And for something a little different, Bakersfield College's new quarterback literally traveled around the planet to wear a Renegades uniform. It's a reminder that even in a city as rooted in tradition as Bakersfield, the community keeps finding new connections to the wider world — and that local sports can draw talent from anywhere.

## Coming up this week

There are a few public meetings worth putting on the calendar. The Police Civil Service Commission meets this morning at 8:30 a.m., and the Personnel and Processes Committee follows at noon — both are open to the public for those keeping an eye on city administration. Looking ahead, the Planning Commission meets tomorrow evening, Thursday, September 3, at 5:30 p.m., which could matter to anyone tracking development proposals across the city and county.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a busy run ahead. This Friday, September 4, catch "The Oldies Night: A Night of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies," followed by Talib Kweli — one night only — on Saturday, September 5. Next week continues with Justin Willman's "One for the Ages Tour" on September 10, Max Amini live in Bakersfield on September 12, and Clay Walker's "Doin' What I Love Tour" on September 13. It's a strong stretch of shows, and with tickets likely to move, it's worth checking the Fox's schedule soon.

Also running through the end of September is that Hageman Road construction — expect daytime delays and plan alternate routes if you travel that corridor, especially during commute hours and school drop-off times. The city says it wants to thank the community for its patience and warns of unannounced delays if unexpected weather occurs.

Have a steady Wednesday, Kern County. Take an extra few minutes on the road, check on your neighbors in the heat-affected corners of the valley, and we'll see you back here tomorrow morning.
